deep.reconstruction:
Context: this is a heavily corrected draft written on a printed postal-ledger form (columns No / Auslage / Porto / Franko). It belongs to the part of Riemann's 'Theorie der Abel'schen Functionen' (Crelle 54, 1857) that shows a function single-valued on the branched surface T is a root of an algebraic equation F(s,z)=0. The previous page is a draft of the letter to the editor accompanying the paper. The next page begins the converse: determining the branching of a root of a given irreducible equation F(s^n, z^m)=0.

Setting. T is a connected n-sheeted branched covering of the z-sphere. s is a single-valued function on T. It is finite everywhere except at m points ε_1, …, ε_m, counted with multiplicity, where it becomes infinite of first order. At a branch point ε the order is counted in the local uniformizer, so a pole there counts in 'Ordnung' relative to the winding of T. The opening lines (heavily struck) set up these conditions: s is finite for finite z, unbounded only at the listed points, with the behaviour at branch points stated separately.

Step 1 (symmetric functions). For a non-branch value z, let s^(1), …, s^(n) be the n values of s on the n sheets above z. Every elementary symmetric function of these values is a single-valued function of z on the plane. It has only poles, at the projections z_1, …, z_m of the points ε. Hence it is rational in z. Therefore (σ − s^(1))(σ − s^(2))⋯(σ − s^(n)) is a polynomial of degree n in σ whose coefficients are rational in z.

Step 2 (pole bookkeeping). The coefficients can become infinite only at z = z_1, …, z_m. Near a point ε that is not a branch point, the factor (σ − s^(i)) carries a simple pole in z − z_i. At a point ε where T winds (a branch point), the local parameter is (z − z_i)^{1/k}. A first-order pole of s there contributes only to a fractional power, so the factor z − z_i appears to a lower power. The page says, in effect, 'In der That ... auf einen Punkt ε, der ein Verzweigungspunkt ist ...'.

Step 3 (clearing denominators). Multiply by the common denominator (z − z_1)(z − z_2)⋯(z − z_m) = k_0 + k_1 z + … (the 'k_0 + …' written on the page). Then a_0 (σ − s_1)⋯(σ − s_n) becomes a polynomial F(σ, z), entire in both variables, of degree n in σ and degree m in z. The degree m in z holds because the product is finite for all finite z and grows at most like z^m as z → ∞. Riemann treats the special case explicitly: if s is finite for all finite z and infinite of order m only at z = ∞, the coefficients are polynomials in z ('ganze Function m-ten Grades von z'). Hence F(s, z) = 0 identically on T.

Step 4 (irreducibility). F is either irreducible ('unzerfällbar') or a power of an irreducible polynomial. Suppose F = F_1 F_2 with F_1, F_2 not powers of a common factor. Then on T the product F_1(s,z) F_2(s,z) vanishes everywhere. Because T is connected, one factor would have to vanish in one part of T and the other in the rest, which is impossible for analytic functions. Hence one factor vanishes identically. Repeating the argument shows F is a power of one irreducible polynomial. The power is >1 when s does not separate the sheets, i.e. when s takes the same value on several sheets over generic z.

The last lines ('durch wiederholte Multiplicationen …', 'unzerfällbaren Function von s können sich …') start the remark about the multiplicity of the irreducible factor. This leads into the next page's converse problem.
errors: No mathematical error is visible in the legible parts. The argument that F is irreducible or a power of an irreducible implicitly uses the identity theorem on a connected T (a product of analytic functions vanishing identically forces one factor to vanish identically). This is standard and acceptable.

The degree count 'm in z' requires counting poles at branch points in the local uniformizer. When some ε lie over z = ∞, only the finite z_i enter the denominator. The draft is aware of the branch-point issue but the legible text does not fully spell this out.

results.what: A single-valued function s on an n-sheeted connected Riemann surface T with m poles satisfies F(s,z)=0, where F is a polynomial of degree n in s and m in z, obtained as the product over sheets of (σ − s^(i)) times the cleared denominator.
results.modern_name: Every meromorphic function on a compact Riemann surface is algebraic over C(z); characteristic polynomial / norm of s over C(z), with degree bound by the number of poles.

results.what: Because T is connected, F(s,z) is irreducible or a power of an irreducible polynomial.
results.modern_name: The characteristic polynomial of an element of a field extension is a power of its minimal polynomial; connectedness corresponds to irreducibility.

results.what: A function finite for all finite z and infinite of order m only at z = ∞ gives coefficients that are polynomials in z ('ganze Function m-ten Grades').
results.modern_name: Integral elements over C[z]; elements of the integral closure.

deep.surprise_reason: This is a working draft of material printed in Riemann's 1857 Abelian functions paper (the section on algebraic functions determined by the surface T). It is of interest only as a draft revealing his phrasing and how he handled branch-point pole orders; it contains no new result.

checkable.sympy: w2 = z**3 - z; expand((z-a)**2*(sigma**2 - w2/(z-a)**2)) - expand((z-a)**2*sigma**2 - z**3 + z) == 0
checkable.asserts: For s = w/(z-a) on the 2-sheeted surface w^2 = z^3 - z, the cleared product over sheets is F(σ,z) = (z-a)^2 σ^2 − z^3 + z.
The degree in z of F equals m = 3, the number of poles of s: two over z = a, plus one at the branch point at infinity counted in the local uniformizer.
The degree in σ equals the number of sheets n = 2.
The product (σ − √z)(σ + √z) = σ^2 − z is irreducible, matching connectedness of the 2-sheeted surface.
If s = z on a 2-sheeted T (s does not separate sheets), the characteristic polynomial is a square of an irreducible polynomial: the 'power of an irreducible' case.

transcription_corrections: Right margin: the '161' is a later archival foliation number, not part of the mathematics.
'(z-z_1)(z-z_2)⋯(z-z_n) = k_0 + …': the index should probably be m (the number of poles), since the following line speaks of order m; the last subscript in the image is unclear.

'Für … Function s von z, die nur unendlich [von der ersten] Ordnung wird' and 'ganze Function m-ten Grades von z' read as stated; 'Zahlwerthe' is likely 'Zahlenwerthe' or 'Verzweigungswerthe' (uncertain).
'F(s/z)' should read F(s,z); the 'n … m' above it indicates the degrees in s and z respectively.
Bottom line: likely 'durch wiederholte Multiplicationen … entstehende', referring to F as a power of an irreducible factor.
